title: Autoscaler leadership flap causing slot starvation and gradual tenant throttling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple Dedicated autoscaler controllers experienced rapid leader-election flaps during a regional control-plane partial outage, which resulted in transient double-reconciliation and premature reclamation of reserved GPU slots. Customers observed gradual request throttling and increased tail latency as headroom was reclaimed incorrectly, triggering several support escalations.
timeline: 2025-02-12 03:12 UTC: Pager alert - Reserved-pool headroom dropped below safety threshold for eu-west-1. Initial automation attempted emergency scale-up but allocations failed with 'assigner: no leader' errors.
2025-02-12 03:18 UTC: Support ticket opened by three customers (AcmeHealth, Notifyly, FinPulse) reporting elevated 429s and long queuing for dedicated capacity. On-call engaged (Luca).

2025-02-12 03:40 UTC: Triage call - found frequent leader election events on autoscaler controller (events in k8s: leader-election lost/won every ~20s). Observed reconciliation loops that marked 'pending allocations' as timed out and released reserved slots back to pool incorrectly.

2025-02-12 04:05 UTC: Hot mitigation - temporarily increased leader-election lease to 60s via feature-flagged config to reduce flaps (runtime flag: autoscaler.leaderLeaseOverride=true). Also applied emergency patch to make pending allocations sticky for 2m during controller transition.
2025-02-12 05:30 UTC: Customers reported partial recovery; 429 rate dropped but tail latency still elevated for larger seq-length workloads. Continued monitoring on dashboard (link below).

2025-02-13 09:00 UTC: Root cause investigation kickoff. Collected logs, metrics, and etcd latency traces. Reproduced leadership-flap locally by introducing transient etcd read latency and network partition between controller replicas.

2025-02-14 14:22 UTC: Engineering review: identified two contributing bugs: (1) reconciler exponential backoff reset on every leader change causing aggressive aborts of pending allocations, (2) allocation state machine allowed 'released' transitions during leadership handoff window.
2025-02-15 11:45 UTC: PR opened with fix for sticky allocations and idempotent reconcile (PR #4012). Warm rollout plan prepared to avoid further churn.
2025-02-16 06:10 UTC: Rollout to canary region (staging + one eu-west-1 shard). Observed no leader flaps and no incorrect reclamations across 48h canary window. Metrics stable.
2025-02-18 09:00 UTC: Preparing backport to runtime-1.18 and internal runbook updates. Drafting customer communications and post-incident report.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy autoscaler controller with >=3 replicas in k8s cluster and enable reserved-pools feature.
2) Introduce transient etcd read latency (simulate with tc/netem 200-400ms for 30s) or disrupt network connectivity between controller pods.
3) Submit a steady stream of allocation requests that consume headroom and create 'pending allocations' (e.g., 50 concurrent allocation requests for a small reserved pool).
4) Observe frequent leader-election events in controller logs and watch allocation state transitions. Verify that pending allocations time out and reserved slots are moved to 'available' prematurely.
5) See customer-facing effect: increased request queuing and 429 responses once headroom is exhausted.
Notes: reproduction requires simulating the control-plane jitter seen during the incident; non-faulty etcd typically does not surface this behavior.
mitigation_actions: - Emergency config change: leader-election lease extended from 15s -> 60s (feature-flagged).
- Hotfix deployed: pending allocations are now sticky for 2m across leader handoffs to avoid premature reclamation.
- Manual customer workarounds provided: temporarily increase reserved pool headroom or enable burst-override for affected tenants.
- Support comms: proactive status updates sent to impacted customers; offered credits for degraded windows.
- Monitoring added: new alert for 'allocation-release-rate' and leader-election frequency per-shard.
root_cause_summary: The incident was caused by leader-election flapping of the autoscaler controller during transient control-plane latency. Two defects amplified the impact: the allocation reconciler reset backoff and timed out in-flight allocations on every leader transition, and the allocation state machine permitted a 'released' state during the handoff window. Together these caused headroom to be reclaimed incorrectly and left tenants with insufficient burst capacity.
action_items: ENG-86210-A: Merge and backport idempotent allocation reconciler fix to runtime-1.18 (owner: Luca) - due 2025-02-22.
ENG-86210-B: Implement stronger leader election health gating (owner: SRE) - add preflight check to avoid resigning leaders during transient etcd spikes.
ENG-86210-C: Update runbook with explicit 'leader-flap' path and customer communication templates (owner: On-call lead) - due 2025-02-20.
ENG-86210-D: Add integration test that simulates leader handoff with pending allocations (owner: Platform QA) - estimate 3 points.
ENG-86210-E: Post-incident customer follow-up with impacted tenants and propose credits / capacity adjustments (owner: Customer Success).
